_schema.products: keyed by the canonical product name vendor.detect_vendors returns (lowercase)
_schema.owner: who ships the product; an advisory counts only if this owner's artifact is affected
_schema.repo: the official source repository, when there is one
_schema.components_unnamed: the vendor's advisories never name a component, so "<component> in <product>" cannot narrow them; the console says so. Read by app_1._unfocused_components
_schema.upstream: the product whose engine this one is built on, so its component CVEs apply here too (Edge: chrome). A "<component> in <product>" question also lists the upstream's component CVEs, tagged as upstream and display-only. Read by app_1
_schema.name_requires: words an advisory must contain to be about this product, for a name that is also an ordinary word (Edge: VAPIX Edge, AMD Versal AI Edge). Also prefixed to the live NVD keyword search. Read by decide._lacks_required_word
_schema.not_this_product: names that sit in this product's advisory subjects while another vendor owns the affected artifact; read by decide._owns
_schema.kev_vendors: CISA KEV vendorProject strings (lowercase) that ship this product; a KEV row from any other vendorProject is not this product's. Read by decide.kev_owns
_schema.kev_products: extra words in a KEV product field that name this product (Chrome is filed as 'Chromium V8', the Windows kernel as 'Win32k')
_schema._not_here: aliases live in vendor._ALIASES and subreddit->product in vendor._SUBREDDIT_VENDOR; not duplicated
